design.rationale: Accuracy deductions come from internal contradictions, not from false platform claims: superseded ARC/UI positions remain normative in four sections (F-04); a schema admits an executor backend that the forwarding rules make impossible (F-02); the callback_descriptors CHECK forces false materialization claims (F-03); 'pinned plan' versus 'rejected with stale_contract' (F-08); container/deployment labels misstate the APK's interactions and the CallbackFlow view is consistent with a forbidden protocol reading (F-01, F-12, F-13); the same class carries disjoint contracts across code views and the design-doc class table uses a different vocabulary (F-11); two reason-code grammars (F-14); 'or'-joined delete semantics and a credential-kind rule that contradicts its own separation claim (F-15); an ARC identifier of unverified provenance presented as what existing clients use (F-18). Completeness deductions: no model path for tools/call dispatch, resources/subscribe/read, cancel and cleanup (F-01); concrete-class callbacks unclassified (F-03); subscription transition table for death/lease/timeout absent (F-07); health tuple and AppBar status element never specified once (F-09); paired-ADB ownership, client realization and deployment topology (F-10); pairing message sequence and TLS host candidate (F-06); negotiated direct stream is a placeholder (F-17); envelope 1.0 vs package 0.8.0 absent from inspected text (F-18); storyboards cover three of the required flow families with placeholder panels (F-19); canonicalization unpinned for cross-language hashes (F-16); toolchain pins incomplete for the determinism claim (F-20). Credits: every requirement has a specified mechanism in prose except the direct stream; protected-owner authentication, pairing proof, Binder acquisition routes, backpressure, startup reuse, lease renewal, admin-route gating, brightness range, MCP resource/journal semantics and ARC framing facts were verified consistent across independent slices and the pinned proto. Scores are not averaged across workpapers; each is a single judgment of the whole design.

findings.prior_issue: At component, dynamic and class level the model cannot trace tools/call dispatch, resources/subscribe, resources/read of finite journal pages, callback.cancel, or execution of the recorded cleanup/unregister plan against the OS; the single read-related edge points from broker to server. The dynamic view as drawn omits the final JSON-RPC response and the subscribe step, which is consistent with the forbidden reading that the POST stream stays open to carry callback updates. The prose (callback section, round013 callback.status/cancel contracts, events_uri status document) specifies these paths, so this is a model accuracy and completeness defect, not a missing mechanism.
findings.working_resolution: Finite registration -> separate subscribe/read/cancel; recorded cleanup OS edge

findings.prior_issue: adb forward carries only host-to-phone connections, and the two channels that could let the phone reach a host adb server (adb reverse, exposing 5037) are prohibited, so the phone-resident bridge has no execution path through a remote host. A connection profile with backend_kind=external_adb is therefore not executable for screen.state/input.tap, yet nothing ties executor_kind=adb to backend_kind=self_adb; the mode is listed as a backend while its description is ingress only. Separately, a client arriving through adb forward presents the host-side Host header (127.0.0.1:<host port>), which fails an exact match against the bound endpoint whenever ports differ; S3 defines no loopback-literal acceptance rule and 'automatic remote tunneling' can be read as excluding the required mode.
findings.working_resolution: Forward is ingress only; exact forwarding authority, no arbitrary loopback Host

findings.prior_issue: (a) Rows with role proven_non_callback or unknown must still carry one of four registrable/abstract-class strategies, so the schema stores a false materialization claim for every non-callback and unknown candidate. (b) Concrete non-final callback classes with overridable no-op methods (reviewer examples: ConnectivityManager.NetworkCallback, WebViewClient) require subclassing exactly as abstract classes do, but no value or reason code covers them; the only available labels are factually wrong for them, so requirement 7's 'ALL callback roles' classification is incomplete.
findings.working_resolution: Role-aware none/unknown and concrete/abstract unsupported subclass taxonomy

findings.prior_issue: Two contradictory normative positions on ARC coexist; schema names, the module table, the screen table and traceability rows do not reflect the internal Kotlin port or the final screen set; the blanket override clause leaves a reader of an earlier section unable to know it is void; the heading implies verification the text disclaims.
findings.working_resolution: Replaced optional-only ARC decisions; current Kotlin ownership and migration vocabulary

findings.prior_issue: The quiesce covers only bridge-dispatched ARC/ADB input. Hosts already authorized by adbd can inject input into any window, including an Ask approval that the chosen profile does not protect with BiometricPrompt, so SCR09 overclaims and the trust boundary is unstated. The mechanism that keeps protected pixels out of shell screencap is unnamed. How the prompt result is bound to nonce/command/scope (CryptoObject-backed key versus an in-process token under the stated single-process trust model) is unstated. The model shows the facade committing directly to the repository with no statement that commit verifies the capability's command hash and expected revision.
findings.working_resolution: Mandatory fresh auth, exact command/revision consume, foreign privileged controller boundary

findings.prior_issue: Not stated: how the agent obtains the server nonce (challenge step or QR payload), how the bootstrap secret reaches the agent and its lifetime relative to the pairing window, HMAC input order and encoding, whether the owner prompt precedes or follows the proof (the 60 s nonce and 30 s prompt interact differently per ordering), and which fingerprint approval binds (only the server has a certificate). The only named engine candidate's TLS capability is explicitly unverified and no TLS-capable candidate is named, so the mandatory pairing route has no named implementable host. 'paired' names both the manual bearer profile and POST /pair, and the manual profile exists only implicitly through 'credential reveal'.
findings.working_resolution: Exact owner/nonce/proof ordering and named SSLServerSocket candidate; runtime spike explicitly gated

findings.prior_issue: Requirement 7 names death, revocation, disconnect and restart. States and some triggers are defined but no transition table: callee/Binder death, lease expiry, registration timeout, the 'failed' outcome and the resulting cleanup disposition are unstated, so two implementers would build different state machines. The declared callback.status input lacks the cursor and limit that list mode requires, and requested_lease_seconds is optional although renewal requires a 1..300 value.
findings.working_resolution: Closed transition/cleanup table; required renew arguments and bounded list cursor/limit

findings.prior_issue: A pinned plan cannot also be rejected with stale_contract after admission, and a dispatched Binder or ADB operation cannot be revalidated. The phases admitted-not-dispatched, dispatched, and live handle are not distinguished, so inflight semantics required by requirement 8 are contradictory as written.
findings.working_resolution: Distinct pre-dispatch/pinned-result/live-handle semantics; publication authority checked

findings.prior_issue: Requirement 2 requires a running-status AppBar/notification and separate MCP, ADB and device-view health. States used elsewhere are missing from the enumerated set, the health dimensions vary between two and three, device-view readiness is not a surfaced dashboard health field, and the AppBar element a storyboard relies on is never specified.
findings.working_resolution: One closed health/status tuple and read-only chip on every SVG screen

findings.prior_issue: The ADB path is attributed both to InvocationPlanner and to ArcEngine with its own OS edge, contradicting the class-level statement that generic phone control is a backend separate from ARC. No component or class owns the single adbd pairing/session, its health, or the ADB TLS client, and whether the client is a bundled adb binary (as in [S17]) or a Kotlin implementation of the wireless-debugging protocol ([S18]) is unstated. The reference deployment shows neither adbd nor the remote host and forwarded ports that requirement 3 defines. 'Locked' has no transitions and verification_strength/identity_verification_method have no CHECK domains.
findings.working_resolution: Kotlin coordinator/native AOSP adapter choice, Locked transitions, paired-peer domains and topology

findings.prior_issue: Requirement 10 demands detailed classes with ownership, multiplicity and responsibility matching C4 components. The same class carries disjoint public contracts depending on the block read; ARC authorization is a second gate not shown converging on canonical policy (requirement 5); the frame and log stream services are unreachable; a transport composing many registries contradicts registry semantics; prose-specified mechanisms have no owning class; and the design document and code views describe the same layer under two unrelated vocabularies with no crosswalk.
findings.working_resolution: Authoritative class views, service/connection lifetimes, policy convergence and vocabulary crosswalk

findings.prior_issue: The container and deployment views misstate the APK's interactions (only journal appends and probes). The owner facade cannot reach lifecycle health, subscriptions, device refresh or audit; ClientAuthenticator has no persistence or audit path although requirement 2 places client mapping in SQLite; refresh on catalog publication (requirement 6) and restart reconciliation (requirement 7) have no trigger edge; the UI->ArcClientAdapter edge contradicts the bounded-facade claim; three direct writers contradict the single-writer ownership label; the ComposeTargetAdapter root's owning component is ambiguous.
findings.working_resolution: Explicit container summaries, owner/auth/catalog/lifecycle/invalidation relationships

findings.prior_issue: Requirement 9's single final JSON-RPC response, requirement 5's per-client grant as a distinct authority, requirement 7's returned finite handle and requirement 4's one-request/stream/terminal semantics are not shown as sequences; a label inverts a query; views are success-only; the static label calls a plan admitted before admission.
findings.working_resolution: Ordered finite results, separate resource lifecycle, group CAS, startup and new failure paths

findings.prior_issue: Requirements 1 and 6 require explicit unknown/unreachable/private/OEM reasons. Two incompatible code formats with overlapping meaning (NON_SDK_BLOCKED versus backend_unreachable:non_sdk) coexist with no closed list or emitting-layer mapping. No reason or policy exists for targets invisible under package-visibility filtering (reviewer recollection: API 30+ requires <queries> or QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES), for exported services guarded by a permission the bridge lacks, for wireless debugging unavailable without Wi-Fi (reviewer recollection), or for inventoried members not on the bridge classpath.
findings.working_resolution: Layer plus stable code grammar; package visibility/permission/classpath/Wi-Fi reasons

findings.prior_issue: (a) Two ETag names for one entry with no stated relation. (b) Two mutually exclusive delete behaviors joined by 'or'; the first lets any remote session block an owner mutation. (c) Admin credentials are literally rejected only at tools/call, so kind=admin can initialize sessions, list tools and read resources, contradicting the stated credential-kind separation. (d) The source of the pre-POST 'independently trusted manifest', the staged handle's lifetime and how an admin client learns it are unstated, so the sequence is not executable as written. (e) In the supporting contract a global generation inside every resource ETag turns per-resource CAS into a store-wide lock and defeats 304 revalidation; If-None-Match on a collection POST, replayed-cursor 410 and lost-response DELETE retry are non-standard or non-retryable. (f) Read-only opening of an untrusted SQLite file does not neutralize schema SQL (views, triggers, generated columns) and no schema allowlist is stated.
findings.working_resolution: Exact tombstone/route/staging/import trust and SQLite allowlist; metadata item PUT and retry semantics
findings.disputed_subclaims: meta1 global-generation ETags are conservative false conflicts by design, not an HTTP prohibition; public representation includes the ETag. DELETE412 after prior successful effect is idempotent by intended effect, not identical response. Cursor replay is allowed. Item creation changed to PUT If-None-Match:* (genuine defect).

findings.prior_issue: The Kotlin service must recompute ETags and content hashes and verify immutable import hashes produced offline in Python. Key-order unit, number rendering, string escaping and Unicode normalization are unpinned, and the canonical signature form (JVM descriptor versus .NET-shaped api.xml names) is undefined, so entry IDs and hashes are not reproducible across languages; the same member could receive two IDs or two members collide.
findings.working_resolution: Explicit canonical bytes and stable language namespace/JVM equivalence separation

findings.prior_issue: Requirement 7 asks for an explicitly negotiated optional direct stream with fallback. The design states constraints on a future mechanism but not the negotiation vehicle, opt-in request, authentication, bounds or fallback signal, so the requirement is deferred rather than designed.
findings.working_resolution: Negotiation, authenticated route, journal cursor/retention/bounds and fallback designed

findings.prior_issue: (a) 'arc-protobuf-v1' is presented as the name existing clients use, with unverified provenance; (b) the required envelope 1.0 versus package 0.8.0 distinction is absent; (c) the target's response to a received Cancel(8) request (UNSUPPORTED status envelope versus close) is unstated and the method name implies the server closes; (d) DIP/density semantics on Compose are undefined; (e) per-event-kind delivery path and the Avalonia key-name map location are unstated; (f) proto3 zero-value handling (empty protocol_version/request_id, method 0, unserialized end_of_stream=false) is unstated; (g) stale marker after abnormal termination and token regeneration per bind are unstated; (h) frame bound and invalid-length behavior are not in the codec contract; (i) version-mismatch behavior across the three protocol_version fields is unstated.
findings.working_resolution: Pinned constant evidence; exact envelope/default/cancel/frame/DIP/input/marker/version semantics
findings.disputed_subclaims: arc-protobuf-v1 is defined by the actual upstream constant, not an invented profile. Reviewer suggested length<=0 reject would break upstream zero-frame semantics; preserve codec zero and reject default envelope at validation. Exact pinned source evidence supplied.

findings.prior_issue: Requirement 12 requires ordered storyboards with screen panels, user actions and success/error/cancel branches for clients/grants, catalog/groups/job discovery, callbacks/events, logs, ARC, settings/boot/backends and protected owner flows. Pairing, grant editing, credential revocation, local override and log export have defined controls and error states but no storyboard; panels are placeholders not bound to control or state IDs; one step is an MCP-client experience framed as an owner action; one success step sits on the failure screen.
findings.working_resolution: 11 screens,5 ordered storyboards,21 slides; concrete actors/control/state IDs and branches

findings.prior_issue: Requirement 11 requires pinned deterministic dependencies and explicit offline/cache failures. The Structurizr CLI digest, Node version, container runtime and the PlantUML layout engine for exported C4 views are not verified or named by the build; the skinparams property is not known to be honored by the Structurizr exporter, so font and background determinism is unestablished; SVG bytes depend on host fonts and JDK while a checksum manifest is produced; UI SVG generation is not a task; count thresholds admit a missing asset.
findings.working_resolution: Exact existing renderer/JDK/Node/Marp hashes, manifest asset set, strict offline failure and Gradle inputs

findings.prior_issue: Unstated: 404 for an unknown or expired Mcp-Session-Id and the client re-initialize rule; MCP-Protocol-Version missing/unsupported handling; whether argument-schema violations are JSON-RPC -32602 or isError; that GET SSE is implemented and how notifications queue while no stream is open; disposition of a result whose POST stream closed after admission and the meaning of 'caller deadline' (no MCP carrier); the carrier of idempotency_key; case/charset rules for subscription_id in the URI authority position; the error code for foreign or unknown URIs; 'exact ... template' is self-contradictory.
findings.working_resolution: Session/header/error/GET/hint queue/disconnect/deadline/URI/idempotency rules

findings.prior_issue: capabilityGeneration semantics are unstated (an owner's UI resume could invalidate the approval they came to grant); a rule whose schema_hash no longer matches the active view is inert by the deny rule but its 're-grant required' surfacing and any automatic rebinding when only graph_digest changed are unstated; 'approvals' versus consumed registration consent needs 'pending (unconsumed)'; 'entry-point tool' is undefined; 'interrupted' and 'reserved' are not permitted states; fingerprint derivation and length are undefined; whether admission fails closed when the mandatory audit append fails, and whether optional log writes run outside the admission gate, are unstated.
findings.working_resolution: Semantic generations, inert stale rules, no auto-rebind, audit/log ordering and stable fingerprint

findings.prior_issue: Logical versus physical display ID mapping between screencap and input (reviewer recollection: screencap -d expects a physical ID, input -d a logical ID) and the minimum Android version are unstated; coordinateSpaceVersion is referenced but never defined; no per-client cap on retained capture references; the source of the admitted target's bounds for the ADB backend is unstated; disposition of an absent or non-integer brightness setting is unstated.
findings.working_resolution: Logical/physical proof, explicit transforms/bounds/capture cap and typed brightness anomalies

findings.prior_issue: Two captions link one file (no dynamic view for generic Binder dispatch exists in workspace.dsl); promised editable source is absent; an API level is written as a version; required transport/binding is missing from the MCP edge; 'initially' hedges the single-process commitment; a numeric claim is off by one GiB unless the reserve is counted; traceability rows read as completed verification when extracted; titles leak markup; small screen-spec inconsistencies.
findings.working_resolution: Correct links/API-version language/units/budget/phase labels; no raster replacement

findings.prior_issue: Each item is a small unspecified detail or naming inconsistency that would be resolved differently by two implementers but does not change the architecture.
findings.working_resolution: Added missing table/ownership/index constraints, memory budgets, boot path and local/meta callbacks
